articles.title: Disney+ and Hulu App Merger Slated to Be Complete in December
articles.summary: Disney's years-long effort to unify the Disney+ and Hulu apps is "nearly complete," Mouse House execs said, as the company looks to concentrate its streaming firepower on the Disney+ platform. Disney ‘s years-long effort to unify the Disney+ and Hulu apps is “nearly complete,” Mouse House execs said, as the company looks to concentrate its streaming firepower on the Disney+ platform.

The company made the announcement in reporting earnings for the September 2026 quarter .

Beginning this December, Disney+ and Hulu bundle subscribers “will have a fully unified experience on Disney+, including live TV and select premium add-ons, creating a more seamless way to discover and engage with the breadth of content across our brands and franchises,” CEO Josh D'Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston said in their quarterly letter to shareholders. “We believe our continued focus on product and technology will yield further benefits in engagement and churn over time.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Former NCT Member Lucas Wong Makes Acting Debut in Taiwanese Folk-Music Drama 'A Time' With Jerry Yan, Ning Chang at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 'African Kung-Fu Nazis' Franchise Lands at Hong Kong’s Cappu Films for International Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

Also in December, Disney expects to begin introducing creator content on Disney+ through its recent agreement with TikTok . The TikTok content rollout will be “strategically aligned” to the lead-up to Marvel's “Avengers: Doomsday” theatrical premiere on Dec. 18, according to the Disney execs.

“We are also adding more vertical video, live sports and podcasts to the [Disney+] platform, while continuing to explore other emerging content genres,” D'Amaro and Johnston said.

Disney's integration of Hulu and Disney+ kicked off in 2023 under then-CEO Bob Iger , two years before the company closed its deal with Comcast to buy out NBCUniversal‘s one-third stake in Hulu in June 2025.

Disney has not announced a sunset date for the Hulu app, and as of now Hulu stand-alone subscriptions in the U.S. continue to be available. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This September, Disney announced another round of streaming price hikes , its fourth rate increases in as many years. The pricing strategy is aimed at pushing consumers toward bundles: The Disney+/Hulu Premium bundle increased two dollars, from $19.99 to $21.99/month, which is nearly half what it costs if you purchase them separately, while the ad-supported Disney+/Hulu bundle remained unchanged at $12.99/month (just 50 cents more than each of the services purchased individually).

According to Disney's D'Amaro and Johnston, ESPN “plays an important role in the overall Disney portfolio by contributing live and on-demand offerings to Disney+, lifting engagement and supporting revenue growth, and encouraging users to upgrade to the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN bundle.”

This fall, Disney increased the volume of sports content we offer Disney+ subscribers without the need for an ESPN subscription. That has included the simulcast of “College GameDay” on Disney+ and adding more live college football games and select NFL games, which kicked off with Dallas Cowboys vs. Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 26. Following the expansion of ESPN content into Europe and select Asia-Pacific markets this year, ESPN now reaches consumers through Disney+ in about 100 markets.

articles.title: Disney Quarterly Revenue Rises 16% and Profit Doubles; Company Forecasts $3 Billion in Annual Cost Savings by 2029 Including Through Layoffs
articles.summary: Disney had a robust quarter, topping Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines. But CEO Josh D'Amaro, who's been in the job for eight months, sees an opportunity for the company to become even more efficient and help fuel future growth. For the three months ended Oct. 3, 2026, which is Disney's fourth […]
articles.content:
Disney had a robust quarter, topping Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines. But CEO Josh D'Amaro, who's been in the job for eight months, sees an opportunity for the company to become even more efficient and help fuel future growth.

For the three months ended Oct. 3, 2026, which is Disney's fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Mouse House reported revenue of $25.95 billion, up 16%, and a doubling of net income to $2.61 billion. Total operating segment income rose 43%, to $4.97 billion. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.77. On average, Wall Street analysts expected revenue of $25.16 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.68 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Kamen Rider' Studio Toei Frames Generative AI Rules, Sets First Video Games for 2027 'Lord of the Rings,' 'Avatar' VFX House Weta FX Partners With Taiwan’s Moonshine Studio Under AI Pact With TAICCA

Overall, it was a solid quarter across Disney's entertainment, sports and theme parks businesses. But D'Amaro and his lieutenants are looking to make Disney leaner and meaner. In their letter to shareholders accompanying the results, D'Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston provided an update to their “efficiency program to create incremental capacity to drive growth,” an initiative that has encompassed several rounds of job cutbacks in 2026.

“We now expect the program to realize annual run-rate operating expense savings of about $3 billion by fiscal 2029,” the execs wrote. “While these efficiencies will be used primarily to fund future growth, we do expect a portion to drop to the bottom line over time.” Disney is poised to make a significant round of layoffs in the current quarter, affecting thousands of employees, with some managers reportedly told to cut expenses by 20% on an annualized basis . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In addition, the execs said, they expect cash content spending in fiscal 2027 of approximately $26 billion, up about 9% from fiscal 2026. That includes “our increased investment in international programming and sports rights, and the timing of feature film production spend,” D'Amaro and Johnston said.

Disney noted that its fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 results had one additional week of operations (a 53rd week) compared with the year-earlier period. The company estimates that the 53rd week contributed approximately 17 cents to full-year adjusted earnings per share.

Revenue from Disney+ and Hulu rose 22% to $5.13 billion in the September 2026 quarter, and operating income more than doubled to $824 million. Disney said it expects to complete the integration of Disney+ and Hulu before the end of 2026 , with a “fully unified experience” available in December.

Starting with the December 2026 quarter, Disney will stop reporting operating income for Disney+ and Hulu. “We have made strong progress scaling our SVOD businesses and, as a result, see a long runway for growth and margin expansion at Disney Entertainment,” D'Amaro and Johnston wrote in the letter. “We no longer believe the supplemental disclosure of SVOD operating income reflects this segment focus and strategy.”

In another financial reporting change, Disney as of Q1 of fiscal 2027 will provide additional revenue disclosures for Disney Entertainment, to “provide greater visibility into how we monetize Entertainment content across distribution platforms, third-party licensing and consumer products,” the company's execs said.

In the September quarter, Disney's Entertainment segment overall saw revenue increase 17% to $11.89 billion. Operating income in the segment shot up 92% to $1.33 billion “due to growth in subscription and affiliate fees and higher content sales, partially offset by increased programming and production costs.”

The execs touted the company's intellectual-property flywheel between theatrical and streaming movie releases. Disney-Pixar's “Toy Story 5,” which raked in $1.15 billion globally at the box office this summer, premiered on Disney+ on Sept. 23, and garnered 20 million views in its first five days on the platform. According to Disney, August was the highest month ever for Marvel Studios viewing, fueled by the summer theatrical success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” (released by Sony Pictures) and the debut of the “Avengers: Doomsday trailer.” During the quarter, Marvel content viewership on Disney+ more than doubled compared with its historical baseline. “Our successful rerelease of ‘Avengers: Endgame' in late September also showed how anticipation continues to build for ‘Avengers: Doomsday,' which arrives in theaters December 18,” D'Amaro and Johnston said in the letter. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At ESPN, revenue increased 16% to $4.61 billion. Growth in subscription and affiliate fees came from an increase of 8% from the additional week of operations in the quarter compared with the year-earlier period, 6% from higher rates and 4% from Disney's deal with the NFL giving the league a 10% ownership stake in ESPN.

Disney Experiences revenue hit $10.11 billion in the September quarter, up 15%, with 5% of the growth in theme park admissions sales coming from higher average per capita ticket revenue. Segment operating income increased 20% to $2.25 billion. Disney Experiences saw an 11% increase in global visitors in the quarter (or a 4% increase excluding the 53rd week). “We continued to see headwinds from lower international attendance at our domestic parks in the quarter, but as expected, those headwinds moderated from the year-over-year impact observed in the third quarter,” D'Amaro and Johnston said.

For fiscal 2027, Disney is expecting double-digit growth in adjusted EPS (excluding the impact of the 53rd week in '26). The company forecast total segment operating income growth of approximately 8%, factoring in the exclusion of equity income reporting from entertainment segment operating results. Disney expects the majority of its growth in total segment operating income and adjusted EPS for fiscal 2027 to occur in the first half of the fiscal year.

In fiscal '27, Disney expects capital expenditures of approximately $9 billion “as we continue to execute against our strategy to turbocharge growth at Disney Experiences,” the execs said. The company invested $8.7 billion parks, resorts and other property in the 2026 fiscal year.

In August, Disney closed the sale of its 50% stake in A+E Global Media to co-owner Hearst for $1.2 billion in cash. For fiscal 2026, A+E contributed approximately $390 million in equity income to Disney's Entertainment segment operating income.

Also Tuesday, Disney's board declared a cash dividend of $2.00 per share payable over the course of fiscal 2027, a 33% increase over the $1.50 per share paid to shareholders during fiscal year 2026.

articles.title: Christopher Hampton on AI – ‘I’m More Interested in Real Intelligence'– and Dos and Don’t’s of Screenwriting
articles.summary: “The least they could do,” Sir Christopher Hampton said about Glenn Close’s Honorary Oscar at the Tallinn Film Festival where at a masterclass, “From Stage to Screen, The Art of Adaptation,” the two-time Oscar winner delivered sometimes trenchant takes on AI – ‘I’m more interested in real intelligence' – and how screenwriting was like gambling […]
articles.content:
"The least they could do," Sir Christopher Hampton said about Glenn Close 's Honorary Oscar at the Tallinn Film Festival where at a masterclass, "From Stage to Screen, The Art of Adaptation," the two-time Oscar winner delivered sometimes trenchant takes on AI – ‘I'm more interested in real intelligence' – and how screenwriting was like gambling at a casino.

"It's about time!," Hampton said of Close's Honorary Oscar."I was very happy to hear that. I think she's still hoping to get one for acting in a specific role, but that hasn't happened yet, so the least they could do was giving her an Honorary Oscar, I guess" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'African Kung-Fu Nazis' Franchise Lands at Hong Kong’s Cappu Films for International Sales (EXCLUSIVE) Alien Cat Sent to Conquer Earth Goes Soft for Catnip and Canned Tuna in Taiwan Creative Content Fest Animated Series 'Operation Maomao'

Unpacking a list of dos and don'ts for screenwriting, using AI was definitely not on the to-do side. In fact, he couldn't care less about the topic.

Comparing AI to "a sort of super Google," Hampton said "AI hasn't troubled me very much. I'm more interested in real intelligence, and I think the flaw in artificial intelligence is in the name because it's artificial."

Asked whether he thought AI could replace screenwriters he said: "I don't think it's gonna happen, as ‘our ‘work is more interesting than ‘its' work." And for those newcomers tempted by writing a script with the help of AI he said: "You're being lazy by allowing some other some other external force to take over you; you might as well choose a different profession."

In fact, at the opening session of the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event's training program Discovery Campus, Hampton who is also juror at the festival's official selection, warned newcomers about the hardships of screenwriting and of works actually landing on screens. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Writing for film is really like going into the casino, he said. "You sit at the table, you put your money under 20 and the chances of the film being made the way you imagined are so tiny that when it does happen, it's incredibly, incredibly fulfilling and it gives you an enormous amount of pleasure. But most of the time, the croupier just takes the chips away and that's it!!"

He said aspiring scribes should accept the fact that "there's a lot of wastage in writing. A lot of projects that you will spend six, nine months or a year writing, will never be seen in any form because somehow, they haven't been financed."

Numerous of his works have never been filmed, he admitted, despite his stellar career as playwright, screenwriter, translator and director spanning five decades that earned him multiple nods and a knighthood for services to drama,

Hampton mentioned an adaptation of the life of Dmitri Shostakovich, "his struggles as a composer in the Soviet Union," written three-four years ago. "I haven't been able to get it made because people don't want to engage with or don't want to make a film about Russia, set in Russia, dealing with Russians. I find it paradoxical because of course it's just the time when it would be interesting to see a film about a man who struggled his whole life with the political system and somehow found ways to circumvent all the roadblocks that were put in his way," he added.

Similarly, another project set in Indonesia in the 1950s, against the background of a conflict between fundamentalist and moderate Muslims, was rejected by financiers due to the topic viewed as problematic at the time, just post 09/11.

He also underscored that many of his works have taken years – sometimes decades – to turn into features. "My projects are very, very slow," he acknowledged, citing David Cronenberg's "A Dangerous Method" that took 14 years, and his directorial debut "Carrington" (a double winner at Cannes 1995) 18 years from script to screen. As for the anticipated "Embers" starring Ralph Fiennes and Viggo Mortensen, Hampton said the screen adaptation of Sándor Márais's acclaimed novel, lined up for 2027, has been 20 years in the making. "I finally got it made with the director I wanted, the great Hungarian director István Szabó," he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"You just have to be patient!" advised Hampton who still hopes that some films that have been waiting 30-40 years might still be picked up, such as the David Lean adaptation of Joseph Conrad's 1904 novel "Nostromo," which was shelved partly due to the director's failing health and eventual death in 1991.

Unpacking the art of screenwriting, Hampton said Lean, the Oscar-winning British director of "Lawrence of Arabia "was together with the legendary Fred Zinneman ("High Noon," "From Here to Eternity") two filmmakers who had determining influences on him.

Having started in 1973 with the adaptation of Ibsen's "A Doll's House," starring Anthony Hopkins, he said it took him more than a decade to fully grasp the difference between writing for theatre – something that came easily to him – and writing for film. "I didn't realise that moving from a stage play to a film was more than simply repeating the dialogue in front of a camera. And it took me about 10 years to figure out how not to make a film from a play which smelt like the theatre."

The mistake he made was thinking that it was easier to write films than theatre plays, he reckoned. "In other words, you think a film gives you enormous liberty, you can jump from London to Hong Kong in one cut, but that liberty imposes on you a number of constraints that I hadn't been aware of before," he said.

From working with Lean, he learned "how to make a scene flow into another, even if it's in a different location or a different subject," and he learned to respect "a film's cohesion, although it might be cut into several chapters like a novel.

From working nine months with Fred Zinnemann ("High Noon," From Here to Eternity") on a project about the last days of WWII – eventually cancelled following a change of boss at 20th Century Fox, he learned to focus on "telling the story, just the story."

After his collaboration with Lean and Zinnemann, Hampton said he went straight to working on Stephen Frears' " Dangerous Liaisons ." "For the first time after 10-15 years of writing screenplays, I felt like I kind of knew what I was doing."

Cronenberg was another visionary filmmaker who had an impact on him and from whom he picked up how to be "more economical," something he then applied for instance while writing the first draft of Florian Zeller's "The Son (2022). "The first thing I did was cut 20 pages!" said the screenwriter who insisted on keeping a story to its core. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"One of the most important skills that you can achieve as a screenwriter is to know what you need to say and don't say any more than that. It's really a question of defining what's essential," he noted.

Expanding on the subject, he said that some filmmakers unnecessarily, feel the urge to over-explain, underestimating the audience "who is always more intelligent than people imagine." He said U.S. Studios with their numerous notes, often ask him "to explain this or that," things that "are there in the script already that they haven't noticed."

Hampton went on criticising Hollywood's formula filmmaking, blockbusters based on universes, that "actually I find completely incomprehensible," he admitted. He also pointed at the U.S. studios' aversion for ‘original' works. He said during a test-screening of his 2003 "Imagining Argentina," one of three works he directed, when a young member of the audience described the film as being original "the [studio] executive next to me put his face in his hands and groaned because there's nothing more difficult for them than something that's original."

Similarly, Hampton dismissed today's TV drama, after being asked by Variety if he was tempted by the format. Unlike in the 1970s, when he would write "a lot" for the BBC when they would produce two to three TV plays and films a week, he said he wasn't tempted by what he calls "a brutal medium" today. The last series he worked on was "The Singapore Grip" which aired on ITV in 2020.

"It took me such a long time, and there were so many notes to negotiate from the people making it. I just thought television really wasn't worth it anymore," he said. While acknowledging that television "provides an enormous amount of work for writers" today, he described the form as probably "the most constricted, prescriptive and unimaginative." "I don't really understand why the freedom that we used to have when I was young – and was very lucky to have –~ no longer exists," he stated.

articles.title: 3 Fantasy Movies That Were Too Ambitious For Their Own Good (& Suffered For It)
articles.summary: Humans have been telling fantasy stories since long before movies even existed, but the big screen has given us a platform to do so better than ever. Many of the best fantasy movies have indelibly imprinted themselves on our collective pop culture consciousness, with their stories and characters becoming beloved in their own right. As […]
articles.content:
Across the history of the genre, many fantasy movies have been punished for trying too much too soon. Filling a fantasy movie with attempts to build a wider mythos prematurely can go against it, as can attempting to establish a world much bigger than the movie's story necessarily warrants. While that sort of ambition deserves to be celebrated, if it comes at the detriment of the movie in question, then it tends to backfire pretty spectacularly.

Guy Ritchie's many career successes made the announcement of his adaptation of classic Arthurian legend seem especially exciting. With Charlie Hunnam cast as the hero King Arthur, the movie seemed to have the potential to be a true fantasy epic. This could easily have been an amazing fantasy movie , but a few creative missteps ruined its chances. Ritchie leaned into his familiar crutch of using English gangster-movie dialogue, and filled the film with visual-effects-heavy action sequences that tried to establish it as the entry point to a new world of supernatural fantasy. This might have even worked, had it not been marketed as an adaptation of the familiar legend of King Arthur, which meant it also needed to establish the many key figures and ideas associated with the legend alongside its original fantasy ideas. Trying to balance it all in a single movie simply didn't work, affecting the film's pacing and ultimately contributing to its poor reception.

2007's The Golden Compass can be best described as a forgotten fantasy movie that tried to start a franchise and failed miserably. Based on the first novel in Philip Pullman's complex His Dark Materials fantasy trilogy, Northern Lights , The Golden Compass attempted to establish the huge scope of the story in its opening chapter. Introducing parallel universes, religious authoritarianism, and mysterious scientific phenomena as part of its story all in the first movie was a lot, and it killed any chance of a franchise before it ever even got itself going. Trying to bring the entirety of Northern Lights to life on the screen simply felt like a jumbled mess, and the one thing that the movie sacrificed was the source material's controversial religious themes, which ironically was perhaps the worst thing to leave out. The result was a movie that tried to do far too much all at once, but also robbed itself of the main source of narrative depth in the novel.

Mortal Engines is perhaps best characterized as science fantasy, but it's another movie that was too ambitious for its own good. The fantasy movie from the 2010s adapted Philip Reeve's novel of the same name, a task which in itself was hugely ambitious. Telling the story of colossal mobile cities that hunt and consume smaller settlements was never going to be an easy thing to accomplish, and the 2018 movie couldn't quite pull it off. While Mortal Engines succeeded in bringing many key aspects of the original story to life on the big screen, so much attention was given to fitting everything in that the film's central adventure felt dull and formulaic, and its characters seemed underdeveloped. It seemed designed to set up a franchise of movies, but in the pursuit of this ambition, Mortal Engines forgot that the first film needed to be successful in order to get audiences invested. In that regard, the movie's ambitious nature served only to work against it, killing the planned franchise before it even began.

"But as soon as I walked in, they asked, How are you with blood? They then gave me a hat and scrubs, and I went in," Findlay recalls. What Findlay saw that day informs part of her next feature, Do No Harm .

The film follows Anna, a young doctor, who accepts a voluntary night shift away from her family on Christmas Eve. When her mentor, Dr. Petersen, is called away, Anna is left in charge of an overstretched maternity ward. With the pressure mounting, she has to make a series of urgent, critical decisions way beyond her experience. Just as things seem to be under control, Anna realises she's made a tiny and very human error that may end up costing a patient her life.

Findlay says the experience of giving birth to her son initially sparked the idea to explore a story set in the world of healthcare.

"I felt the experience was as close to being in a thriller as I could have imagined," she says. "It's like being on a train that was impossible to get off. There was a sense of being in a relentless present tense, with no way out of the experience except through it."

Findlay cites Sebastian Schipper 2015 feature Victoria as a thematic inspiration, but says the project fits into a substantial gap in the market she has identified around the representations of childbirth in contemporary filmmaking.

"I felt there weren't many representations of labour and childbirth that really spoke to that visceral, thriller-like feeling," she says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"So often, the images we see of childbirth and labour are essentially cozy. Often they're from a male perspective: you can run through the familiar images in your head, like somebody's waters breaking in a supermarket. I'd never seen anything that captured the sense of it as a reckoning with mortality."

Findlay is best known in international film circles for her debut feature Midwinter Break (2026), written by Nick Payne, and starring Lesley Manville and Ciarán Hinds. The feature premiered at the Glasgow Film Festival before a theatrical release via Focus Features. However, Findlay is also one of the UK's most prolific theatre directors. Her recent productions include Alma Mater (Almeida Theatre); White Noise, A Number (The Bridge); Rutherford & Son, Beginning and Middle (National Theatre), and The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie (Donmar).

Do No Harm will mark the first time Findlay has directed a feature from a screenplay she has also written.

"I started writing to work out what the idea was, and as I kept writing, it acquired its own momentum and became something I felt able to write," Findlay says of the process.

"I'd always wanted to write something, and I've spent a lot of time in the theatre working on new writing. I suppose that, over time working in theatre, I'd built up a kind of toolkit by osmosis."

Findlay says she has "two really brilliant actors" attached to play Anna and Dr. Petersen, but cannot yet disclose who they are. Financing is still underway.

"We're hoping to shoot next year," she says. "The BBC has been behind the project from the very beginning. It's BBC Films, Fable and Hinterland Productions, and MK2 is doing the sales for us."

Findlay added: "We've got a really great team and a lot of pre-sales happening, so I think it will happen."

articles.title: 40 Years Ago, Tom Cruise Starred in a Sequel That Predicted Hollywood's Obsession With Legacy Sequels
articles.summary: It may be wild for modern audiences to believe, but before the current prominence of the legacy sequel, Hollywood used to just move past certain movie franchises if too many years had gone by without significant movement on a sequel. While the world of horror, for instance, has been able to put a different actor […]
articles.content:
Certainly, the advent of the internet and, with it, the ability to constantly lean into the nostalgia of past entertainment is a part of it. Another element is the development of de-aging technology that can shave decades off of 80-year-old Harrison Ford for over 20 minutes of Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny. But the real trend behind never letting franchises truly die is the explosion of the legacy sequel. With every film franchise from Star Wars to Rocky rebranding with a next-generation lead, it’s easy to think this concept is a new development. But in truth, Tom Cruise starred in one of the earliest mainstream examples of a legacy sequel 40 years ago.

In 1986, Cruise was only a few years into his acting career. He had made his film debut in 1981’s Endless Love and had a breakthrough year in 1983 with the triple-header of The Outsiders , All the Right Moves , and especially Risky Business . But just three years later, he shared the screen with Paul Newman in The Color of Money . Directed by Martin Scorsese, the film served as a sequel to the 1961 release The Hustler , which starred Newman as a small-time pool hustler named “Fast Eddie” Felson. That film became a critically acclaimed classic, but Hollywood didn’t move forward on a follow-up until 25 years later.

In The Color of Money , Newman returns as Felson, who comes across a young man named Vincent Lauria (Cruise). Recognizing his skill at playing pool, Eddie and Vincent hit the road for a six-week road trip of pool hustling. The Color of Money earned Newman the Academy Award for Best Actor, the only Oscar the legendary star won during his career. And mirroring the on-screen mentor-mentee relationship, the film can be easily read as one iconic movie star anointing the next. After all, Cruise has been a defining screen presence ever since, and intriguingly enough, The Color of Money hit theaters the very same year as Cruise’s star-making Top Gun .

As fans well know, Cruise’s brush with the legacy sequel didn’t end with The Color of Money . In 2022, he returned as Pete “Maverick” Mitchell — the role he originated in 1986’s Top Gun — for the long-awaited sequel, Top Gun: Maverick . For more than a decade, a follow-up to director Tony Scott’s original film was in the works, and by the time Cruise and director Joseph Kosinski made it, the project had turned into a bona fide legacy sequel. The twist is that this time Cruise was the elder statesman to a new generation of pilots, with Miles Teller playing the son of his late best friend Goose. But no one could have expected how warm a reception the film would receive.

Top Gun: Maverick was more than a hit when it arrived in theaters; it became a full-fledged phenomenon . With an older, wiser version of Cruise’s Maverick at the center, the movie carried a gravitas that propelled it to a whopping $1.5 billion at the worldwide box office and six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture. It’s remarkable to see how The Color of Money and Top Gun: Maverick represent two very different sides of Cruise’s career, and they certainly make intriguing companion pieces as, respectively, one of the earliest legacy sequels and one of the most successful examples of it done right.

Which franchise would you like to see get a legacy sequel? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: How Sky Studios Elstree Built for the Future
articles.summary: Managing director Noel Tovey on starting a lot from scratch with sustainability, accessibility, training and community at its core — and opening its stages to the entire industry.
articles.content:
Sky Studios Elstree, while in its infancy, has put down roots to outlast all of its peers.

Opened in 2022, this 27.5-acre studio in Borehamwood, Hertfordshire, has 12 sound stages ranging from 10,000 to 40,000 square feet, a six-acre backlot and sprawling production offices, workshops, prop stores and dressing facilities. But even while the studio's slate of star-spangled projects continues to grow and its reputation for large-scale innovation is steadily nurtured — you might be shocked to learn Jonathan Bailey's attempt to collect dinosaur DNA wasn't actually shot on a cliff edge on a remote island in the Atlantic Ocean — the team here prides itself most on what audiences don't see. Built around four key pillars of sustainability, accessibility, training and community, getting up to speed on Sky Studios Elstree (not to be confused with the nearby, entirely separate Elstree Studios) is not unlike stepping into the future: This is a studio that has harnessed the power of a post-pandemic birth to meticulously design and construct a lot that will continue to thrive for decades, if not centuries, from now.

Below, Tovey dives into those aforementioned pillars and talks about welcoming the entire industry — not just their own commissions — to Sky Studios Elstree. Wuthering Heights , the success here isn't just raising the bar for rivals, but letting everyone take a share of the (sustainably made) pie.

Sky Studios Elstree is not just a studio for Sky projects, is it?

No, so primarily, we were built as a facility to [accommodate for] in-house production. Sky have got a big slate. As do our partners at NBCUniversal and all the companies that they own or have a financial stake in. And I think it was felt — and this was before I joined Sky, so I'm surmising the discussions here — but I think it was felt that because of the boom in production activity [and] the advent of the streamers coming to London in a big way, the Netflixes and Amazons and what have you, all the existing studios and stage space got swallowed up very quickly. It gave us the opportunity to look at construction methods [and] look at trying to be as light [as possible] on carbon use. For example, the concrete use in the stages here is minimal, and where we do use it, it's as low-carbon as possible. And then, thinking afresh, we knew that we were going to put solar panels on the roof, so you build the roof structure to be able to take that [with] all air source heat pumps. Building a studio from scratch meant that we could take advantage of all the technologies that we could see coming, and also make the site easy for productions to use. And from my experience, productions, by the time they get to us, they have a schedule. Once they arrive, they've got a delivery date. They're working back from that. What is that commitment to sustainability rooted in, in the context of the ethos at Sky?

On paper [and] from the start, it was going to be the most sustainable studio facility we can possibly build. It was designed from the ground up. We've got 140,000 square feet of solar panels on the roofs, for example. We envisaged quite a lot of crew may have electric vehicles, so we over-delivered car charging in their multi-storey car park. We probably got more than we need, but we were building for the future. For example, all the buildings and stages are super-insulated, which does well for sound insulation, but also heat retention, or in the summer, cooling retention.

Do you get good feedback from the talent about the sustainability features in place?

The talent, I don't know how much they know [about what] we're doing. ( Laughs .) But certainly from the productions, and also when a production has to submit their sustainability card to [BAFTA Albert Studio Sustainability Standard], for example, you've already got an Albert scorecard for the studio at 95 percent just by being here. You tick a few of their scorecard boxes, and then we handle the waste management. Zero waste is going to landfill from us. Everything that can be recycled is recycled, so it's very easy to track. We can give data and reports of that waste journey.

Could you talk a little bit about the projects that you attract?

We've got some very large sound stages. Because they're so large, you need a certain size of production that requires them, and that tends to be set-built [projects]. [With] Wicked , that was obviously an imaginary land. They did go to shoot some locations, like the fields in Norfolk with the tulips and what have you, but the rest of it was thought up in the directors' and production designers' minds. So you need a huge, voluminous soundstage in which to create these sets, and we've got those. That, by default, [is] the type of [productions] that tend to come to Sky Studios Elstree. We did the last Jurassic [ Jurassic World Rebirth ] here. We've got quite a large back lot, and any shows that need a good back lot set… So Paddington shot here, and they had quite a big element of water work, so they built some boats on gimbals. I hope I'm not giving away the secrets behind the cameras. ( Laughs .) But they'll shoot some of the stuff on location, then they'll come and do the really technical, difficult bit back with us, where you can control the environment 100 percent. I don't know if you've seen the last Jurassic , but they build that huge cliff on the back lot — where they've got to take the DNA from the pterodactyl egg.

You need to change all the crowd, get them through hair and makeup. Then you need to all go for lunch somewhere that's big enough to cater for them and the crew. […] And I must say that I've seen a move since Wicked [where] directors want to create things in camera and not to rely too much on visual effects in post. I also wanted to ask about the talent programmes you have, and how Sky Studios Elstree is trying to cultivate the next generation of film and TV craftspeople.

We're doing a lot. We were lucky to have all the learnings and all the infrastructure that Sky had from Sky Up in their center. So [now] we have a Sky Up Academy here, and school children come along. We do a classroom in the morning, a classroom in the afternoon. Prior to arriving here, they've been sent a pack to their school, and they work through the different projects that they can do. And and ultimately, they come here and they make a little short movie in a little XR studio that we've got, and as part of that, they learn about all the jobs behind the camera.

And just to digress for a moment, there was a thought that virtual production was going to be huge and nobody will need scenic backings anymore. Well, most of the stages here right now, all their backings are scenic-painted, which is fantastic to see. Over the years, they became green and blue, and then virtual, and now they're going back to scenic, and it's a dying art. Brad Pitt was enthusiastic last night on The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth when he was asked about Amazon MGM confirming Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond .

Indian actress, director and social advocate Nandita Das and Syrian star Taim Hassan are set to be honored by the Doha Film Festival with Creative Excellence Awards during the event's opening ceremony on Thursday.

She's subsequently worked with top Indian directors such as Mrinal Sen, Shyam Benegal, Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Rituporno Ghosh and Mani Ratnam. articles.title: John Malkovich Sets West End Return With Rosalind Eleazar in 'History'
articles.summary: The production is the West End debut of playwright Rebecca Reid.
articles.content:
John Malkovich is returning to the West End for the first time in 30 years.

Hot on the heels of immense Oscar buzz for his latest outing in Martin McDonagh's festival favorite Wild Horse Nine , the Oscar nominee will co-star with Rosalind Eleazar in a production of Rebecca Reid's History .

The play is set to mark Reid's West End debut, and will have a limited run at Wyndham's Theatre from May 17 to Aug. 7 2027. It follows Wren, who once had a vibrant, creative life until motherhood, sleepless nights and doomscrolling took over. On a reckless whim, she invites James — the ex who once defined her — to lunch. Their reunion forces Wren to reconsider a relationship she believed belonged firmly in the past. “I couldn't be more delighted to start work in the months to come on this fascinating new play, opposite Rosalind Eleazar and directed by Matthew Dunster,” Malkovich said this week about coming back to the London stage. “I can't wait. Rebecca Reid has written something rare — a play that is complex and profoundly human.”

Malkovich has wowed audiences this year as a terminally ill CIA operative in the buddy-comedy Wild Horse Nine opposite Sam Rockwell. He's also known for roles in Being John Malkovich , Dangerous Liaisons , and In the Line of Fire .

articles.title: 5 2010s Sci-Fi Movies That Gen Z Grew Up With, But Are Virtually Unwatchable a Decade Later
articles.summary: Every era has movies they grew up with that they watched over and over, only to later realize that they aren't quite as good as they thought. These films are still sure to have a special place in the hearts of those who grew up with them, even if they're pretty unwatchable today. Millennials and […]
articles.content:
That doesn't give them a lot of time to age poorly or to become unwatchable, yet it still happens. The best place to find movies like this is in the sci-fi genre. The 2010s were riddled with attempts to bring popular young adult fiction or sequels in major franchises to the big screen. These films were hits at the box office or when rented by Gen Z, yet we can look back at them and realize that they weren't totally worth watching as often as people did. Trying to watch them again today opens your eyes to their many problems.

Everywhere you looked in the 2010s, a new sci-fi young adult novel series was being adapted into a movie. The Hunger Games was the most successful, while the likes of The Maze Runner performed less favorably, yet still did well. Divergent felt like it could be the second biggest attempt at this, set in a dystopian world where people are divided into factions based on human virtues. The story follows Beatrice (Shailene Woodley), a Divergent who doesn't fit into any faction and ultimately helps uncover the truth about the world around her.

The books are wildly popular and the 2014 film grossed nearly $300 million. However, as much as many teens may have gotten hooked on the series, the film received lackluster reviews for feeling overly generic and predictable. Despite a talented cast, Divergent isn't great to rewatch like some other YA adaptations, and the sequels are significantly worse, causing the franchise to get canceled before it put out the final installment .

Pixels is exactly the kind of sci-fi movie that so many Gen Z kids grew up with. Released in 2015, the Chris Columbus film spoke to many young people. It was a sci-fi comedy that saw aliens misinterpret footage of classic arcade games as a declaration of war, causing them to attack Earth with recreations from those games. That puts the best video game players on the front lines to combat them.

The always popular Adam Sandler led the way in a film that was a blast upon release, especially for younger viewers. However, it isn't the kind of thing that holds up particularly well. The jokes are too immature to work today and it certainly feels like it earned that poor 17% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Teens can see the PG-13 today and have a good time, but it's not one of those movies that is as fun once you're older.

It might sound odd to anyone who didn't experience it, but there was a time when Sharknado was one of the biggest pop culture talking points around. Released in 2013 straight to the Syfy network, the sci-fi comedy movie plays to its title, as a waterspout bursts and lifts sharks from the ocean, launching them throughout Los Angeles. The movie wears its goofiness on its sleeve and developed a cult following that ultimately led to several sequels over the years.

The over-the-top premise and theatrics are what made the film such a hit. That said, it's the kind of wacky thing that you can have fun with the first time around, yet not quite as well upon rewatches. Sharknado feels like the kind of cultural hit that you had to experience as it happened. Once you know what happens, the fun wears off. If anyone attempted to get into them today, it likely wouldn't work nearly as well.

Hollywood saw the box office success of things like Transformers and decided it needed to try and bring more Hasbro toys to the big screen. Unfortunately, this was a mistake because a lot of them don't translate all that well. One failed attempt was Battleship , based on the board game of the same name. The game has a basic setup of two people trying to sink each other's ships, which doesn't translate to something interesting in a movie format.

2012's Battleship loaded things up with a notable director in Peter Berg and a great cast featuring Taylor Kitsch, Rihanna, Alexander Skarsgård, and more. There are likely plenty of Gen Z kids who had a blast watching this because of the loud explosions, recognizable faces, and action set pieces. Alas, the story is paper-thin, the performances aren't great, and films that are basically all noise don't exactly work when you watch them back at an older age.

By the time 2014 rolled around, the Transformers franchise was a proven box office hit. The previous entry, Transformers: Dark of the Moon , even crossed $1 billion worldwide. It makes sense that millions grew up with Transformers: Age of Extinction , which also surpassed $1 billion. However, this was a soft reboot that brought in new human characters and never quite hit the same way that the 2007 and 2011 installments did.

When looking back at all the Transformers movies , the two starring Mark Wahlberg have a strong argument for ranking near the bottom. Transformers: Age of Extinction is something that probably got viewed a lot by younger audiences during the 2010s, but now that they're older, they can see just how lackluster almost every element is. It's mindless action and while that has its place, there are far better options out there if that's what you're looking for, from the 2010s and even from this franchise alone.

Are there other sci-fi movies from the 2010s that you think fit this topic? Let us know in the comments!

articles.content:
Music generated an estimated INR17,400 crore ($1.8 billion) worth of economic activity in India in 2025, 45% more than two years earlier, according to a new EY study backed by the Indian Performing Right Society ( IPRS ).

Digital platforms accounted for 52% of that value. Combined label and publishing revenue hit a record INR5,433 crore ($563 million) in 2025, up from INR4,938 crore ($512 million) in 2023. Publishing and performance income rose 79% over the same stretch, climbing from INR628 crore ($65 million) to INR1,125 crore ($117 million). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jimmy Fallon Works on Big Plays for NBC's 'Tonight': 'Fockers' After Football, L.A. Indians streamed close to six trillion tracks last year. Independent artists took 43% of digital listening, compared with under 35% in 2023, a shift the report ties to rising appetite for regional-language and artist-driven music.

The report, titled “It Is a Good Time to Be in Music: India's Music Creator Economy Report Vol. 2,” also found that jobs in the organized segment rose 50% to between 60,000 and 70,000. Annual output of original songs climbed to between 22,000 and 27,000. Live is growing too: India staged more than 130 days of concerts in 2025 that each drew over 10,000 people, double the 65 recorded in 2023.

Scale has yet to translate into global clout. India slipped one place to 15th in IFPI's recorded music revenue rankings and sits 23rd for music collections under CISAC. Music revenue per head was $0.40, against $44.70 in the U.S. Of the 233 million Indians who streamed music in 2025, only 14 million to 16 million paid for a subscription.

A survey of more than 5,900 JioSaavn users, conducted with the streamer and focused on Gen Z habits, showed music running through the day. Some 88% listen for at least an hour daily. Travel (85%), relaxing (76%) and work (56%) topped the list of listening occasions, with studying also featuring strongly. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Creators are conflicted. While 75% believe there are more opportunities than before, 76% say those openings are getting harder to exploit. More platforms, direct reach and overseas audiences have arrived alongside unpredictable income, a fight for discoverability, complicated rights administration, higher marketing spend and new risks from AI.

Lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar , speaking at the launch, said the figures left him “very depressed.” Of the roughly INR5,000 crore ($518 million) that reaches the production side, he estimated that composers, lyricists and singers receive less than INR1,000 crore ($104 million). “So something is seriously wrong even today. Seriously wrong,” he said.

The report puts licensing compliance among eligible businesses at around 4%, the same figure Akhtar cited for hotels, restaurants, bars and events. He said he had proposed to the IPRS board that the government add a question on royalty payments to the GST (goods and services tax) form. “So, it's only lack of intention. Lack of intention,” Akhtar said.

“Could you imagine that someday you would need to patent the voices?” Akhtar asked, adding that the family of the late singer Kishore Kumar receives nothing from the many songs now made in the singer's voice, and calling for new international rules to deal with AI.

“India's music economy is creating significant value, but its long-term success will be measured by how effectively that value reaches creators. Strengthening monetization avenues, rights management and export capabilities through creator education can help translate rising consumption into sustainable growth for the entire ecosystem,” said Ashish Pherwani, partner and media and entertainment leader at EY India.

The report's wish list includes better rights awareness among creators, clearer royalty payouts, simpler compliance for shops, venues, events and public spaces, a one-stop licensing window and set rate cards where practical. It also proposes an export promotion council dedicated to music, and calls for closer work between government and industry, more regulatory certainty and formal training in music creation and management. Vasant Sangeet Dwar, the country's first single-portal system for licensing public performances, went live in February 2026. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“India possesses a unique opportunity to emerge as one of the world's leading music markets and cultural exporters. By nurturing talent across languages, regions, and genres, encouraging innovation while safeguarding creators' rights, and building stronger bridges between culture and commerce, we can unlock the full potential of India's music creator economy,” said Lily Pandeya, joint secretary at India's Ministry of Culture.

The findings arrive alongside CISAC's 2026 Global Collections Report, published in the organization's centenary year, which showed music creator royalties worldwide up 11.9%. Digital collections rose 27.9% and now make up 45.6% of the total, while live and background music became creators' second-biggest income source globally.

Youssou N'Dour, vice-president of CISAC (the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers), said India's music scene mirrors a worldwide shift in which creators are reaching audiences at unprecedented scale. “The future of the industry will depend on ensuring that creators have the knowledge, rights and opportunities needed to build sustainable careers and continue enriching our societies through music,” he said.

For a sense of what an export push could deliver, the report points to South Korea, where K-pop generated more than $3 billion in overseas music-led revenue in 2025.

articles.title: Over 400 U.K. Industry Figures Demand End to “Culture of Open Secrets” After Russell Brand Trial
articles.summary: The open letter warns against calling Brand’s 10-and-a-half-year sentence a turning point: “It has taken some 17 years for justice.”
articles.content:
More than 400 U.K. entertainment industry professionals have signed an open letter, released Monday, calling on leaders at studios, broadcasters and unions to end the culture of silence and secrecy that the signatories say allowed Russell Brand 's abuse to go unchecked. Brand was sentenced last week to 10 and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault.

The letter, billed as an "open letter to the creative industry, from the creative industry," comes as Little Britain star David Walliams faces allegations of sexual misconduct. A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News includes accounts from two women who say Walliams groomed them after meeting them when they were 15. Walliams denies wrongdoing. The letter asks those in power to "review your processes, protect those who speak out and become less offended by your inaction being named than you are by the actions you are being asked to recognize." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories General News Brit List 2026: Cornwall Outlaw Series, Coming-of-Age Film Top List of Unproduced Film, TV Scripts Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google"

The letter was written by writer-actor-producer Ben Fletcher, co-organized by Alexa Morden and published on a dedicated website, makethisaturningpoint.com. Signatories include actors, directors and producers such as Natalie Dormer ( Game of Thrones , The Hunger Games ) and Richard Armitage ( The Hobbit ). The letter calls on the government to "act, not debate" by "increasing support for victims, ensuring police forces are fully resourced, and forcing accountability for those who know but choose convenient ignorance."

Brand's sentencing on Nov. 9, after a high-profile London trial in which he testified in his own defense, is a major catalyst for the letter. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the buzzy, David Fincher -directed standalone sequel to Quentin Tarantino ‘s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , held its premiere in Los Angeles on Monday evening and the first reactions have hit social media.

The embargo for full critics reviews for Cliff Booth is Nov. 19, but Netflix allowed some brief social media reaction to the film after its L.A. premiere. Cliff Booth sees Brad Pitt return as the titular character, the effortlessly cool veteran Hollywood stuntman we saw in Once Upon a Time . In the sequel, we see Pitt's character as now more a part-time stuntman who seems to be doing odd, and sometimes dangerous, jobs in 1977 Los Angeles.

The ensemble cast includes Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan , Yahya Abdul-Mateen II , Carla Gugino, Peter Weller , Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis and Karren Karagulian.

articles.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Director Teases Marvel Film Will Make a Big Change From Other MCU Movies
articles.summary: As the clock ticks down for the Dec. 16 release date of Avengers: Doomsday, Marvel Studio's head honchos are already looking ahead to what comes next. Similar to the Thanos arc that culminated with Infinity War and Endgame, Doctor Doom's epic will also take place across two interconnected films, with the latter being Secret Wars […]
articles.content:
With a full month away before the film arrives in theaters, Doomsday is continuing to make headlines as more and more pieces are revealed. Its constantly growing roster of characters is already unparalleled compared to the last two Avengers , with a recent addition of a surprising X-Men character quietly announced last week. On top of that, Hugh Jackman let it slip that Wolverine and Deadpool should be showing up in the movie in one way or another, but like all of these characters, their role (and multiversal location) remain to be determined. With so much happening already, the sequel looks to up the scale to a whole other level.

In an interview with Empire , Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige promised that the upcoming Secret Wars “is a whole other genre of story” to Doomsday . Director Joe Russo added to that, stating that the Doomsday sequel will be “a really unique world” with a “unique story” that will be very different than what we are used to seeing. “The only reason to get out of bed every day is to take risks and surprise people and try things that have never been tried before. I think Secret Wars is one of those movies where I hope people will walk out of it and go, ‘I’ve never seen anything like that in my life!’”

This sounds like Hollywood hyperbole meant purely to sell tickets, but by all accounts — it's working. Without fully knowing what will happen in Doomsday , we can only take guesses based on events from the comic books that could flesh out what a potential movie could be like. If we're following the 1984 Battleworld arc by Jim Shooter, it's going to be a huge Royal Rumble of every hero and villain in the world colliding to see whether the forces of good or evil prevail. At the time when the original comics were published, it was a huge deal to see so many characters crossing over in the same place at the same time. However, we already got a world-encompassing crossover in Endgame , and it feels too soon to repeat the same tactic.

Jonathan Hickman's Secret Wars from 2015 might be the key to solving how it fits into Doomsday and why Feige and Russo feel it's going to be such a change of pace. I'll try not to spoil it too much for folks who would like to read this or wait to see the movie adaptation, but it involves Dr. Doom, multiverses and a whole lot of reality-shifting. It also helped merge a few characters from their Ultimate universe into the 616 world, which raises the question of whether Marvel characters from different studios could be wrapped up into this epic film or which ones we simply haven't seen yet could make their debut in an unexpected way . There's also the chance it revives a few other high-profile characters who haven't been seen in a while or who were killed off (such as Thanos) to give them a shot at redemption or perhaps something else we don't yet understand.

There are many rumors about the events Doomsday depicts, many of which are apocalyptic in nature (not the Oscar Isaac character) and would result in sweeping changes across the franchise. What isn't hyperbole to say is December's movie will be the catalyst of something big for the entire MCU in a way that hasn't happened yet, and if all goes according to Feige's plan, the landscape will truly be reshaped into something we have never seen before.

Do you think Secret Wars can pull off what Feige and Russo have suggested, or are they overhyping things more than they need to? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Kevin Feige Reveals The 6 Words That Led to Robert Downey Jr. Returning to the MCU as Doctor Doom
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Doctor Doom is coming to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, and it turns out that the discussion for this started with six words. It was Kevin Feige who got the ball rolling when he approached Robert Downey Jr.'s agent at a movie premiere and said six words to the man. Feige told him, "We have […]
articles.content:
The new issue of Empire Magazine has broken down the upcoming movie, and it includes the reveal of what Kevin Feige said to start Robert Downey Jr.'s return to the franchise as Doctor Doom . What is most surprising is that Feige said the six words at the premiere of Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania .

Kevin Feige first approached Robert Downey Jr.’s agent at the ‘ANT-MAN AND THE WASP: QUANTUMANIA’ premiere about returning to the #MCU as Doctor Doom with a cryptic message: “We have an idea. It’s time.” (via @empiremagazine ) pic.twitter.com/PBeuwj5wkE

This is interesting timing. When Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania was released, the next Avengers movie wasn't even going to be Avengers: Doomsday . The movie was going to be called Avengers: The Kang Dynasty . The main villain was going to be Kang, and this would lead into Avengers: Secret Wars . In fact, the post-credits scenes in Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania showed the Council of Kangs, and then Kang was a big part of the Loki series on Disney+, setting up the entire idea for Avengers: The Kang Dynasty .

At the time of this discussion between Kevin Feige and Robert Downey Jr.'s agent, Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania hadn't flopped yet. Furthermore, Jonathan Majors was still signed on to play Kang. It seemed like it wasn't until Marvel fired Majors that the movie idea changed to Avengers: Doomsday . In the end, it made sense because it was Doctor Doom who was the man responsible for creating Battleworld in “Secret Wars” in the comics, so he should be the one who did it in the MCU.

However, it also makes sense when you step back and look at the situation. Just because the first movie was Avengers: The Kang Dynasty , it didn't mean that Doctor Doom wasn't showing up as well to create Battleworld. It would be easy to see Kang causing all the problems with the incursions thanks to a new multiversal war breaking out between Kangs. Then, just when Kang was about to destroy everything, Doctor Doom could have stepped in to save the day and create the story for Avengers: Secret Wars . Majors being fired could have just forced Marvel to bring in Doom sooner. Doom was likely planned all along, and it seems that the Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania premiere was when these discussions started.

articles.title: 5 Dead Superheroes Who Took Forever to Come Back to Life
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics In both Marvel and DC Comics, death is frequently treated as just a mere inconvenience. Whenever a superhero dies, they often only have to wait a few months or a couple of years before popping right out of the grave to continue crimefighting. Fan reactions to these resurrections have ranged from excitement to anger. Yet […]
articles.content:
Superhero deaths are always more impactful when they’re given time to rest, and their loved ones have time to grieve and move on. And when these long dead heroes finally return, they find the world has changed in ways they never could have imagined.

1985’s Crisis on Infinite Earths was one of the most monumental events in comic book history , and saw many iconic heroes and villains lose their lives. One of the most stunning deaths of the series was that of Kara Zor-El, aka Supergirl. In Crisis on Infinite Earths #7 , Superman’s cousin tried to destroy the Anti-Monitor to end his multiversal genocide. Unfortunately, the Anti-Monitor gained the upper hand and killed Supergirl. After the Crisis on Infinite Earths , the DC Universe was rebooted, and several new Supergirls were introduced to replace Kara. Instead of Kryptonians, the new Supergirls included a shapeshifting alien robot called Matrix and the human Linda Danvers. Eventually, the original Supergirl would make her climactic return in 2004’s Superman/Batman #8 19 years after she died. Rather than a straightforward resurrection, Kara’s return was DC Comics rebooting her character and origin for the post-Crisis timeline. Since then, Supergirl has once again cemented herself as one of the most important members of Superman’s family.

Along with Supergirl, another significant hero killed during the Crisis on Infinite Earths was the second Flash, Barry Allen. In 1985’s Crisis on Infinite Earths #8 , Barry ran as fast as he could to tear apart the Anti-Monitor’s antimatter cannon so it wouldn’t destroy the five remaining universes. While the plan worked, Barry pushed himself too far, disintegrating into dust and becoming one with the Speed Force. Afterward, Barry’s mantle would be picked up by his sidekick, Wally West , the former Kid Flash. Wally would then be the primary Flash in DC Comics for decades. It would take 23 years for Barry to return officially in 2008’s Final Crisis #2 . In the issue, Barry managed to break himself free of the Speed Force and return to the world of the living after narrowly escaping the Black Racer. Since then, Barry and Wally have taken turns operating as the main Flash of DC Comics.

The Doom Patrol is one of the most underrated superhero teams in DC Comics history. But, in 1968 all its members met a tragic end. Doom Patrol #121 was the final issue of the original series, and with it, the core four members of the Doom Patrol, Robot Man, Elasti-Girl, Negative Man, and the Chief, sacrificed their lives to save a city from being destroyed by a bomb. And while most of the Doom Patrol were eventually revealed to have cheated death, Elasti-Girl was the only one who stayed buried. The shapeshifting hero remained dead for 36 years until the events of 2006’s Infinite Crisis , when Superboy-Prime rewrote all of existence with a reality punch. This event changed Elasti-Girl’s history, so the Chief salvaged a piece of her skull and used it to regrow her body. Although she was initially under the Chief’s control, Elasti-Girl eventually broke free. Now, Elasti-Girl has reestablished herself as a core member of the Doom Patrol.

Few comic book characters have made a more iconic return after their supposed death than Bucky Barnes. Captain America's plucky sidekick, Bucky was presumed dead after Avengers # 4 in 1964. During World War II, the heroic duo tried to stop Baron Zemo’s drone from attacking the Allied Forces. However, the drone was booby-trapped and blew up. The explosion led to Captain America freezing in ice for decades and to Bucky presumably being c killed in action. Bucky’s death became an integral part of Captain America’s character as he was haunted by his inability to save his friend. Yet, in 2005’s Captain America Vol. 5 #6 , Bucky’s death was retconned so that he not only survived but was transformed into the brainwashed Russian assassin, the Winter Soldier. Having been considered dead for 41 years, Bucky’s return was a huge surprise that forever changed Captain America’s lore. Additionally, Bucky has since broken free of his brainwashing and become a hero once again.

The X-Men have suffered many losses over the years, but few deaths were once thought to be more permanent than Thunderbird's. Debuting as a member of the All-New All-Different X-Men, Thunderbird only lasted three issues before he tragically died in 1975’s X-Men # 95 . In the issue, the X-Men battled the villain Count Nefaria. When he tried to escape in a jet, Thunderbird’s stubbornness led him to jump onto the jet and tear it apart until it exploded, killing him. Since then, Thunderbird only made brief appearances as an undead soldier or a spirit. However, that would all change 46 years later in 2021’s The Trail of Magneto #5. At this time, the mutant nation of Krakoa assembled the Five, a group of mutants who discovered the key to resurrection. Working together, the Five resurrected almost every mutant who had ever died, including Thunderbird. After being brought back to life, Thunderbird would dedicate himself to protecting the Apache people and mutantkind.

articles.title: 5 Dark Fantasy Anime to Watch on Crunchyroll in November 2026
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Crunchyroll The ever-growing popularity of the anime industry has many enthusiasts looking to venture into the world of exciting shows and movies. No doubt, as the world's largest streaming platform for anime fans, Crunchyroll is the one platform fans would go to in order to browse new series. However, the platform is full of over a thousand anime […]
articles.content:
The Fall 2026 anime season kicked off last month, and all major platforms, especially Crunchyroll, have released exciting new shows for fans across the globe. Crunchyroll by far had the biggest anime lineup for the season, just like every other quarter, with new weekly releases to keep fans busy for the rest of the year. However, since the latest season’s anime was released only released last month, there aren’t enough episodes for fans to binge. If you’re looking for new anime shows to watch this month that have already released full seasons, then this list is perfect for you.

Not only is it one of the most famous anime exclusively available on Crunchyroll, but it is also one of the highest-rated isekai of all time. The anime series is based on the acclaimed light novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichiro Ootsuka. Two years after the novel debuted in 2016, the White Fox animation studio released the anime adaptation, which continues to return with new sequels. 2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the anime, and over all these years, four seasons have been released, as the story keeps getting more intense.

The anime is often praised for exciting plot twists, unique worldbuilding, and thrilling action as it centers around Subaru Natsuki, an ordinary teenage boy. After leaving a convenience store one evening, he suddenly finds himself transported into another world. Equipped with the ability to return to time, Subaru tries his best to adjust to the new world while also dealing with any threat that comes his way.

This dark fantasy from MAPPA is based on an older manga which was serialized from 2000 to 2018. The anime shares strong aesthetic ties with gritty details while following a hyper-violent Japanese animation that’s reminiscent of the 1990s. The story takes place in an underground alley called the Hole, which draws heavily from the grimy, pipe-filled, rain-slicked urban dystopias seen in 90s cyberpunk and Seinen anime such as Ghost in the Shell: Memories or Battle Angel Alita . The animation style uses 2D and 3D CG by the studio, but the design philosophy and aesthetics aren’t that different from the cult spirit of the 1990s animation.

The anime debuted in 2000, and it took MAPPA six years to return with a second season this year. A third season has already been confirmed , and fans are awaiting updates on the anime as Caiman and Nikaido get closer to discovering the dark secrets lingering in the alleys of the Hole while also uncovering what transpired in the past.

Puella Magi Madoka Magica is an acclaimed fantasy classic on Crunchyroll with a surprise dark twist beneath its cheerful facade. The story focuses on magical girls and remains one of the most shocking series of all time. The award-winning show released its anime adaptation in 2011 before returning with sequel films in 2012 and 2013. This acclaimed original series follows Madoka Kaname and Sayaka Miki, two middle school girls whose ordinary lives take drastic turns after encountering Kyuubey, a mysterious magical familiar. Kyuubey offers the girls an offer to grant any one of their wishes if they become magical girls.

The girls can gain enough power to fulfill their dreams. However, Homura Akemi, a new transfer student and a magical girl, tries her best to stop them from accepting the offer. She claims that the offer isn’t what it looks like, implying there will be a major price to pay.

However, among the major titles of the season, a new action fantasy series quickly climbed the ranks. Sentenced to Be a Hero caused huge waves in the anime industry after its debut on Crunchyroll as it captured fans’attention with its spectacular animation, unique premise, and promising plot. The anime is not only highly rated but also offers a lot of unique concepts, which make it stand out from the rest. The anime series is based on a light novel written by Rocket Shoukai and illustrated by Mephisto.

This dark fantasy story offers a twisted outlook on the role of a hero since this title is given only to those who have committed the most heinous crimes. While almost all fantasy stories glorify the coveted title of hero, this anime considers it the worst punishment anyone can ever receive. Heroes are those who serve in the military in an endless war against the Demon Lords. However, the worst part is that the convicts aren’t even allowed to die. If they somehow lose their lives in the battle, they will be resurrected over and over again, so they will keep fighting a never-ending war. The resurrection process is brutal since it forces the soul of a hero straight out of hell and puts it back into its corpse.

When it comes to modern anime, specifically those released in the 2010s and 2020s, Attack on Titan ‘s legacy can’t be matched with anything else. Written and illustrated by Hajime Isayama, the manga reached its controversial finale in 2021, which sparked so much fury from fans that the creator was losing sleep over it. Attack on Titan follows Eren Yeager, a boy whose mother is devoured by a Titan when monstrous, humanoid beings breach his hometown’s walls.

This trauma ignites a burning obsession to destroy every Titan. What starts as a survival horror story quickly transforms into political intrigue. From Eren’s ability to transform into a Titan, the origins of Titans, the truth about the attack on Shiganshina during Eren’s childhood, the world outside of Eldia, and, of course, Eren’s true goal, Attack on Titan has been a wild ride at every turn of the story. It’s one of those stories that keeps fans engaged with these twists, as every plot point and foreshadowing starts to make sense after the truth is revealed. However, once things are set in motion, there’s no way of changing what has been done. Is there any series or movie you like that didn’t make it to the list? Let us know in the comments why your favorite dark fantasy on Crunchyroll deserves the spotlight.
